key_insight: A hybridization-derived Interior Penalty Nitsche method combines boundary and interior stabilization for heterogeneous, anisotropic diffusion while providing a closed-form, single-valued numerical normal flux.
engineering_relevance: The formulation supports finite element simulation of diffusion-driven engineering processes with spatially varying and direction-dependent material properties.
method: Derive the formulation from an interior-penalty-stabilized Lagrange multiplier method.
Prove equivalence between the hybridized formulation and its condensed Interior Penalty Nitsche form.
Establish stability and convergence for symmetric, incomplete, and nonsymmetric variants.
evidence_signal: Numerical experiments validate the theory: under stated regularity assumptions, the symmetric variant achieves optimal L2 convergence, while incomplete and nonsymmetric variants lose half an order.
watch_item: Locally conservative H(div)-conforming flux reconstruction remains future work; the available numerical normal flux is a starting point, not a completed reconstruction.
paper_title: A hybridization-derived interior penalty Nitsche method for heterogeneous and anisotropic diffusion
